Candidate C2 (NULL/garbage dereference of pols[i] for i>=2 in the final loop, CWE-476/CWE-125): there is no entry bound on *num_pols in this code (only the ==0 check at the top), so if a caller passed *num_pols >= 2 with uninitialized slots, `pols[i]->action` would dereference garbage; no statement in this code produces or documents that entry state, so the trigger is speculative.

Candidate C3 (reference leak / eventual UAF via overwriting an already-populated pols[1] when entry *num_pols == 2): requires the same unproven caller state; the overwrite-and-leak chain has no instantiated link in the given code.

The behavior of xfrm_pols_put and xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype (refcount semantics, error returns) is external to this code; the call sites here test both observable sentinels (NULL and IS_ERR) before first use, so no unchecked sentinel reaches a sink.

verdict.summary: squashfs_opendir reads directory entries from directory_table at an index (`bytes`) derived from attacker-controlled on-image inode fields ((*i)->offset, (*i)->data) and image content, without ever comparing `bytes` (or `size`) against the actual size of directory_table. The only loop bound is `while(bytes < size)` where `size = (*i)->data + bytes - 3` is itself attacker-controlled, so a crafted squashfs image drives memcpy reads (lines 53/56, 72-77, 86-87) past the end of the directory table buffer — an out-of-bounds read of attacker-influenced length (dire->size + 1).

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read sink: memcpy reads sizeof(*dire) bytes from directory_table + bytes, where bytes is an unvalidated index derived from attacker-controlled inode fields and image content; no statement in this function bounds bytes against the directory table size.

Origin of the unvalidated index: bytes (attacker-influenced lookup_entry result) is advanced by attacker-controlled (*i)->offset and inside the loop, and the loop bound size = (*i)->data + bytes - 3 is also attacker-controlled; the loop condition never compares bytes against the directory table's actual size, so the memcpy at the end of this range reads out of bounds.

assumptions: directory_table is a finite in-memory buffer whose size is smaller than values reachable from attacker-controlled (*i)->offset / (*i)->data / dire->size sums; no code shown bounds these values, so the overread is reachable.
read_inode and lookup_entry return values parsed from the untrusted squashfs image; their outputs are treated as attacker-data since no validation of their range appears in this code.
limitations: dire->size overflowing the local `buffer` was dismissed: the guard `if(dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN) { ... goto corrupted; }` is quoted and lies on every path before the first use of dire->size at the memcpy and NUL write.
dir_count exceeding SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT was dismissed: the guard `if(dir_count > SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT) { ... goto corrupted; }` is quoted and precedes the inner while loop on every path.

verdict.summary: rrlen is declared uint16_t but assigned a size_t sum (strlen(provider_name) + 16 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 2). The only guard rejects strlen >= 0xffff0000 (size_t-scale overflow), not the 16-bit wrap that actually occurs at a provider-name length of ~64866 (config-controlled, unbounded elsewhere). When the true sum is exactly 65536, rrlen truncates to 0, malloc(0) returns a valid zero-size chunk, and snprintf(rr, rrlen - 1, ...) receives (size_t)(-1) = SIZE_MAX, writing the full provider name plus the TXT preamble out of bounds into the heap; subsequent loop iterations and the closing-quote snprintf continue the overflow. Residue 1 (rrlen == 1) additionally makes strlen() read an uninitialized malloc(1) buffer and wrap the next size argument. Heap out-of-bounds write with attacker-influenced content.

evidence.reason: Root cause and sink: the guard on line 40 only rejects provider names >= 0xffff0000 bytes (size_t-scale overflow), but rrlen is a 16-bit variable, so any provider-name length L with L + 18 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) >= 65536 (L ~= 64866 for a 163-byte cert) passes the guard and truncates rrlen. With the sum exactly 65536, rrlen becomes 0, malloc(0) returns a valid zero-sized chunk (only the !rr NULL check exists), and 'rrlen - 1' evaluates to (size_t)-1 = SIZE_MAX, so the snprintf on line 55 writes L+16 bytes of config-controlled content past the allocation. Trigger instantiated: L is unbounded config-read content with no length contract quotable in this code; the attacker chooses L mod 65536 to hit residue 0 (deterministic OOB write) or residue 1 (strlen() over uninitialized malloc(1) memory with a wrapped size argument on the next snprintf).

Origin of the width defect: rrlen is declared uint16_t (line 19) while the value assigned at lines 45-49 is a size_t sum that can legitimately exceed 65535 given an unbounded provider_name; the narrowing assignment is the truncation point that makes the malloc size and every subsequent snprintf size argument unreliable.

assumptions: sizeof(struct SignedCert) is not given in this snippet; the attacker does not need to know it because the provider-name length mod 65536 is fully attacker-chosen, so the residue that makes rrlen wrap to 0 (or 1) is reachable for any compile-time constant C < 16384.

malloc(0) is assumed to return a non-NULL unique pointer (mainstream allocators such as glibc); if it returned NULL the code would return -2 instead of overflowing. The residue-1 (rrlen == 1) variant does not depend on this assumption for its uninitialized strlen() read.
Line 43 'continue' is written without a semicolon (compile error as transcribed); treated as a transcription artifact equivalent to 'continue;'.

dnscenv->provider_name is populated from resolver configuration outside this snippet; per the analysis rules configuration-read content with no quotable length contract in the given code is treated as attacker-data, so no trust-based demotion of the trigger was applied.
limitations: The rrlen == 1 residue (strlen() over an uninitialized malloc(1) buffer, CWE-457/CWE-125, followed by a wrapped size argument) is a second instantiation of the same root defect and is not emitted as separate evidence.
Unchecked return value of cfg_strlist_insert at line 71: failure requires strdup/malloc failure, which is an environment/allocator condition, not attacker-inducible content; recorded, not classified.
provider_name == NULL would crash strlen/strdup at lines 5-6/40, but no statement in this code can produce a NULL provider_name and no quotable contract either way exists; speculative, not a finding.

The cast '(unsigned)strlen(...)' on line 40 could itself wrap for strings >= 2^32 bytes, but such a string is not realistically instantiable and the ~64866-byte trigger already proves the vulnerability at the reachable boundary.

verdict.summary: sug_filltree walks a trie loaded from a spell file (slang->sl_fbyts / sl_fidxs) using fixed-size stack arrays (MAXWLEN) with no bound on either the traversal depth or the child index values taken from the file. (1) depth is incremented once per file-supplied non-NUL byte (tword[depth++] = c; arridx[depth] = idxs[n];) with no depth < MAXWLEN check anywhere, so a trie deeper than MAXWLEN writes file-controlled idx_T/int values past arridx/curi/wordcount and an attacker-chosen byte past tword — a stack buffer overflow. (2) n = arridx[depth] + curi[depth] is derived from raw file index values and used as byts[n] (line 54) and byts[arridx[depth]] (line 37) with no n < sl_fbyts_len check (the only length check, line 77, runs after the first read and only in the c == 0 branch), giving out-of-bounds reads; line 40 likewise writes idxs[arridx[depth]] at an unvalidated file-derived index.

evidence.reason: Stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): depth (an int starting at 0, line 34) is incremented once per non-NUL trie byte with no upper bound; the only loop guard 'while (depth >= 0 && !got_int)' (line 35) checks the lower bound only, and no depth < MAXWLEN check exists on any path. With a spell file whose folded trie contains more than MAXWLEN chained non-NUL bytes, after MAXWLEN descents line 87 writes the file-controlled idx_T idxs[n] to arridx[MAXWLEN] (past the idx_T arridx[MAXWLEN] declared at line 6), lines 88-89 write ints past curi/wordcount, and the next descent writes the attacker-chosen byte c (any value 1-255) past tword[MAXWLEN] at line 86 — memory corruption in this function's own statements.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): arridx[depth] is assigned directly from the raw file value idxs[n] (line 87), so n is fully attacker-controlled; c = byts[n] is executed with no check that n < slang->sl_fbyts_len. The only bound in the function, 'while (n + 1 < slang->sl_fbyts_len && byts[n + 1] == 0)' (line 77), executes after this first read, only inside the c == 0 branch, and does not cover this sink. The same unvalidated arridx[depth] also indexes byts at line 37 ('curi[depth] > byts[arridx[depth]]') on every iteration.

Out-of-bounds write into the heap idxs array (CWE-787, same root cause as the unbounded trie indices): arridx[depth] holds file-derived idxs values with no bounds validation anywhere in this function — no sl_fidxs length is even referenced — so this store can write far outside the index array allocated for the spell file.

evidence.snippet:
byts = slang->sl_fbyts;
    idxs = slang->sl_fidxs;
evidence.reason: Taint origin: the trie byte and index arrays consumed by this function are the serialized contents of a spell file read from disk; every depth, byte, and index decision below is driven by this attacker-derived content, and this function performs no validation of it (no depth cap, no index bounds), making it the last — and absent — line of defense.

assumptions: MAXWLEN is a fixed compile-time constant (arrays at lines 6-9, 13 are sized by it); whatever its exact value, it is finite, so a trie chain longer than MAXWLEN overflows the stack arrays.

sl_fbyts/sl_fidxs and their contents are produced by the spell-file loader (not shown); per GUARD ANCHORING the absence of any quotable bound there cannot be used to dismiss the defects, since the harmful uses occur in this code.
got_int is an external flag set by interrupt handling; not attacker-content.
limitations: spell_soundfold (line 59) and tree_add_word (line 63) are not shown; any overflow inside those callees from tsalword/tword cannot be confirmed here and is not counted.
The words_done >> 16 / words_done & 0xffff split (lines 63-65) relies on the counter not exceeding 2^32; no wrap reachable within realistic input sizes was instantiated.
The exact value of MAXWLEN and the heap layout past idxs are outside the given code; impact is established for the stack-array overflow (candidate C1) via the quoted writes at lines 86-89.

verdict.summary: In squashfs_opendir, the read position into directory_table is computed from unvalidated attacker-controlled inode fields ((*i)->offset added directly, and the loop end computed as size = (*i)->data + bytes - 3). No statement anywhere in the function bounds 'bytes' or 'size' against the actual size of the directory block returned by lookup_entry or the directory_table allocation, so a crafted squashfs image drives SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_HEADER/SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_ENTRY and the memcpy source at directory_table + bytes out of bounds, for an attacker-chosen offset and extent; out-of-bounds heap data then flows into dire->name and is stored into extracted directory entries.

evidence.reason: Root cause and instantiated trigger: (*i)->offset and (*i)->data come from the attacker-controlled inode read at line 17 (*i = read_inode(block_start, offset)) with no validation. bytes += (*i)->offset and size = (*i)->data + bytes - 3 are the only bound on the loop, and they reference no table/block extent. Simulation: lookup_entry returns bytes=100 (not -1, so line 44 passes), offset=5000 gives bytes=5100, data=0x100000 gives size=1064963, 5100 < 1064963 is true, and SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_HEADER(directory_table + 5100, &dirh) reads out of bounds at an attacker-chosen offset. No check of bytes against the directory block or table size exists anywhere in the function (the only checks are dir_count > SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT and dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN, which bound other quantities), so the OOB read at directory_table + bytes is unguarded.

Continuation of the same unguarded sink inside the entry loop: bytes keeps advancing past the directory block/table (bytes += sizeof(*dire) at line 68 and bytes += dire->size + 1 at line 103) with no comparison to the block or table extent, so SQUASHFS_SWAP_DIR_ENTRY(directory_table + bytes, dire) at line 66 and the memcpy source directory_table + bytes at line 76 read out of bounds for every entry once bytes passes the end of the directory block. The quoted guard dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN only bounds the copy into the local buffer, not the read from directory_table. OOB heap bytes read here become dire->name contents and are persisted via strcpy(dir->dirs[dir->dir_count].name, dire->name) at line 97, giving disclosure of out-of-bounds memory in extracted directory entries.

Origin of the tainted position: start is keyed by the attacker-controlled (*i)->start from the inode read at line 17, and lookup_entry returns a block position/length derived from the attacker-built image. The only check on the returned value is the failure sentinel bytes == -1; a successful out-of-range or in-range value flows unchecked into the loop at line 51 whose bound is itself set from attacker data, which is what enables the out-of-bounds reads at lines 52, 66, and 76.

assumptions: The allocation size of directory_table, the semantics of lookup_entry (returns a position/size within the table for a valid key, -1 on miss), and the width of struct dir_ent.name in the destination of strcpy are not shown in this code; none of these are treated as guards (GUARD ANCHORING), and the primary OOB-read finding does not depend on them.

The widths of (*i)->offset and (*i)->data are taken from the on-disk squashfs inode format consumed by read_inode; either width suffices for the trigger (the simulation uses small values well inside any plausible width).
squashfs_opendir processes data from a squashfs image file, an untrusted origin per the data-origin model; no deployment privilege was assumed.
limitations: Unsigned wrap edge in dir_count = dirh.count + 1: if dirh.count is 0xFFFFFFFF, count+1 wraps to 0, the quoted check 'if(dir_count > SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT)' passes, and 'while(dir_count--)' processes one entry before terminating. The check is bypassed at this boundary, but the consequence (reading one unvalidated entry at an unbounded bytes) is subsumed by the confirmed out-of-bounds read; not reported separately.

Attacker-scalable memory amplification: a large (*i)->data (up to ~2^31) can drive up to ~2^28 iterations and realloc growths of dir->dirs before the loop ends; however every such path terminates the process on realloc failure (EXIT_UNSQUASH), the same denial of service already delivered by the primary OOB read, so it is recorded here rather than as a separate finding.

A potential out-of-bounds write via strcpy(dir->dirs[dir->dir_count].name, dire->name) could not be verified because the width of the destination name field is not visible in the given code; the source is provably bounded to SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN by the quoted check at line 71.

The integer truncation size = (*i)->data + bytes - 3 (long long sum stored into int size) can produce a negative size and skip the loop at extreme values (e.g. (*i)->data = 0x80000000); it cannot extend the read beyond what the confirmed finding already provides, so it is merged into the primary root cause rather than reported as a separate CWE-190 finding.

verdict.summary: check_termcode() unconditionally writes a NUL sentinel at tp[len] where len is the valid-input length (*buflen or typebuf.tb_len), while the capacity parameter bufsize is never consulted anywhere in the function; when called with buf != NULL this is a one-past-the-end out-of-bounds write (offset == *buflen reached directly via `if (offset >= *buflen) break;`, which bounds only the data length, not the capacity).

evidence.snippet: tp[len] = NUL;
evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write sink: len is computed as the valid-data length (*buflen - offset for the buf != NULL path, line 48; typebuf.tb_len - offset for the NULL path, line 41), and the write lands exactly one past the last valid byte with no comparison against the buffer capacity bufsize anywhere in the function.

Data-flow origin of the faulty index: the only guard bounds offset against *buflen (valid data length), never against bufsize (capacity), so tp[len] = buf + offset + (*buflen - offset) = buf + *buflen writes one past the last valid byte; a caller-supplied buffer sized to the data length (buflen == bufsize) yields a one-past-the-end write.

assumptions: termcodes[] entries and termleader[] are global terminal-code tables populated elsewhere; their contents are assumed to be configuration-derived, not directly attacker-controlled within this function.

handle_csi, handle_osc, handle_dcs, get_bytes_from_buf, get_long_from_buf, getdigits, decode_modifiers, check_termcode_mouse, and put_string_in_typebuf are not shown; their internal bounds behavior is unknown.

MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN is a compile-time constant bounding `char_u string[MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN + 1]`; no statement in this function ties new_slen to it — the safety of string[new_slen++] relies on modifiers2keycode (not shown) returning <= MAX_KEY_CODE_LEN - 3.
Deployment (terminal-driven editor) is inferred from comments; per discipline 3 it does not affect the verdict since the buf/buflen/bufsize parameters constitute the function's own input surface.
limitations: KS_VER_SCROLLBAR / KS_HOR_SCROLLBAR loops read tp[j], tp[j+1], tp[j+2] with no len check, relying on tp[len]=NUL as a partial sentinel and on get_bytes_from_buf/get_long_from_buf (not shown) to stop; also gated behind FEAT_GUI && !USE_ON_FLY_SCROLL configuration not quotable here — speculative.

KS_MENU path casts raw input bytes to a pointer (current_menu = (vimmenu_T *)val) but immediately validates via check_menu_pointer(root_menu, current_menu); the validation walk is not shown, so the impact chain is not instantiated in this code.

Reads at tp+slen for TABLINE/TABMENU/GUI mouse paths are bounded only by the single sentinel at tp[len] plus non-shown helpers; a multi-byte over-read beyond the sentinel is not instantiated with quotable statements.

For buf == NULL, the write typebuf.tb_buf[tb_off + tb_len] may be within the typebuf allocation by design of the shared buffer (a sentinel slot), but that guarantee is not quotable in the given code; the confirmed defect is the buf != NULL path where bufsize is provably never checked.

verdict.summary: In mobi_parse_index_entry, the raw pointer control_bytes (line 45, buf->data + buf->offset) is advanced once per TAGX tag with control_byte == 1 (line 66) and dereferenced at line 70, with no bounds check anywhere. The loop bound is tagx->tags_count, fully attacker-controlled via the crafted TAGX record of a malicious MOBI file, and is unrelated to the number of bytes remaining in buf. Placing the index entry near the end of the heap buffer and supplying more control-byte tags than remaining bytes makes control_bytes[0] read past the end of the buf->data allocation: an attacker-scalable out-of-bounds heap read (info disclosure into parse decisions, reliable segfault) reachable by any untrusted file.

evidence.reason: Root cause: unguarded out-of-bounds read. The loop bound is tagx->tags_count (attacker-controlled TAGX record), and each iteration with control_byte == 1 advances the raw pointer control_bytes (line 66) with no comparison against buf->data + buf->maxlen; the dereference control_bytes[0] at line 70 then reads past the heap allocation. Trigger fully instantiated: entry positioned at buf->offset = S-10 with buf->maxlen = S passes the line-16 check (S-5 >= S is false), label_length = 0, ten control-byte tags advance control_bytes to buf->data + S + 1, and the eleventh tag reads buf->data[S+1] out of bounds.

Taint origin: control_bytes is initialized as a raw pointer into the buffer (buf->data + buf->offset), deliberately bypassing the bounds-checked mobi_buffer API; the subsequent mobi_buffer_seek moves buf->offset only and provides no protection for control_bytes, whose only later movement is the unchecked increment at line 66.

assumptions: buf->data is a heap allocation of at least buf->maxlen bytes; the line-16 check (buf->offset + entry_length >= buf_maxlen returns) proves buf->offset < buf_maxlen on every path reaching line 45, so the initial control_bytes pointer is in-bounds and only the unchecked increments can push it out of bounds.
INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX is assumed to be at least 255, so the get8-sourced label_length (max 255) fits text[INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX + 1]; the constant's value is not defined in the given code.
idxt/tagx/ordt/buf structures are populated by parsing untrusted file content (MOBI INDX/IDXT/TAGX/ORDT records), per discipline 3.
limitations: Candidate not promoted: strncpy(indx->entries[entry_number].label, text, label_length + 1) at line 42 reads label_length + 1 bytes from the fixed stack buffer text[INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX + 1] with no check of the callee-returned label_length (line 29/31) against sizeof(text); the excess-length precondition is produced by mobi_getstring_ordt/mobi_indx_get_label, whose code is not given, so the trigger could not be instantiated in this code. Note the ORDT branch (line 28-29) also lacks the buf->error check present at lines 32-35 in the other branch.

entry_length = idxt.offsets[curr_number + 1] - idxt.offsets[curr_number] (line 7) can wrap for non-monotonic offsets, but the line-16 sum modulo 2^64 reconstitutes idxt.offsets[curr_number + 1], so no harmful wrap survives the check.

(int) tagx->control_byte_count cast at line 46 could truncate a control_byte_count > INT_MAX; no statement in this code can produce such a value (it is parsed elsewhere and not shown), so this is speculative.
malloc(tagx->tags_count * sizeof(MOBIPtagx)) (line 56) could overflow only for SIZE_MAX-scale tags_count; no shown parse statement can produce that scale.
mobi_buffer_setpos return value (line 8) is unchecked; if the callee clamps/flags out-of-range positions, buf->offset stays in-bounds — callee behavior not shown.

verdict.summary: All array-access and copy sinks reachable within getcmdline_int's own statements are guarded by checks verified in execution order at boundary values: the Ctrl_U copy loop relies on the cmdpos<=cmdlen invariant maintained by the shown K_RIGHT/K_LEFT/Ctrl_E handlers; cmdbuff[cmdpos-1] reads are short-circuit-guarded by cmdpos>0; the depth counter is a balanced unit-step counter with the 'depth == 50' bail-out; mb_char2bytes output is bounded at <=6 bytes into IObuff; init_ccline's failure sentinel is tested before any ccline use. The only unguarded index, wim_flags[wim_index], is incremented exclusively by the not-shown callee cmdline_wildchar_complete, and wim_flags's declared width is absent from the given code, so no concrete out-of-range value can be instantiated from these statements; it is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

assumptions: init_ccline(firstc, indent) returning OK implies ccline.cmdbuff is allocated; this code tests the failure sentinel ('if (init_ccline(firstc, indent) != OK) goto theend;') before first use, which is the quotable guard, but the callee's internal allocation logic is not shown.
IObuff is a file-scope/global buffer whose declared size is not in this snippet; the writes here are bounded to at most 7 bytes (mb_char2bytes emits <=6 bytes plus the NUL) for any int value of c.
wim_flags is a file-scope global not declared in the given code; its element count could not be quoted, so the exact index value that would be out of bounds is unknown.

Unshown callees (put_on_cmdline, nextwild, ExpandOne, cmdline_erase_chars, cmdline_insert_reg, cmdline_paste, bracketed_paste, cmdline_browse_history, add_to_history, showmatches, get_special_key_name) are assumed to maintain the ccline invariants (cmdpos<=cmdlen, NUL termination, capacity); defects inside them are outside this code's statements.
extra_char is a file-scope global not declared in this snippet (assigned NUL in the Ctrl_V/Ctrl_K cases).
limitations: wim_flags[wim_index] (K_S_TAB handler, both uses) is indexed without a bound check in this code. The only shown writes to wim_index are 'int wim_index = 0;' and 'wim_index = 0;' (end_wildmenu block). The incrementing producer is the not-shown cmdline_wildchar_complete(..., &wim_index, ...), and the array's declared width is not in the given code, so the out-of-range trigger value cannot be instantiated from shown statements; the fall-through path (wildchar completion returning a non-CMDLINE_CHANGED result, then c == K_S_TAB with p_wc set to <S-Tab>) was otherwise shown to be reachable. If the callee can push wim_index past the array width, this would be an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125/129) — unverifiable here.

Ctrl_U's copy loop ('while (i < ccline.cmdlen) ccline.cmdbuff[i++] = ccline.cmdbuff[j++];') would overflow if any unshown callee (cmdline_erase_chars, put_on_cmdline, cmdline_insert_reg, cmdline_paste, open_cmdwin) ever left ccline.cmdpos > ccline.cmdlen; no shown statement produces that state.

The depth==50 bail-out ('goto theend' after init_ccline succeeded while did_save_ccline is TRUE) returns the freshly allocated empty buffer while restore_cmdline reinstates the parent's ccline; ownership of that returned buffer is the caller's contract (not shown) — no dangling dereference occurs in this code.

Defects inside unshown callees (e.g., bracketed_paste's handling of terminal escape sequences at 'case K_PS:', nextwild/ExpandOne completion buffer math, add_to_history sizing) cannot be analyzed from this snippet; only in-domain arguments are passed from here.

state->lens, state->codes, window buffers and lencode/distcode tables are sized compatibly by inflateInit/inflate_table (not shown) per the inftrees.h ENOUGH contract.
